securityKey.title: Security key
securityKey.connectHint: Insert it, and unlock it if it asks; this window notices it by itself.
securityKey.helperFailed: Couldn't start the security key helper.
securityKey.keys: Tab moves · Enter activates · Alt+key on a button runs it · F5 refreshes · Esc closes
securityKey.touch: Touch the key when it blinks…
securityKey.fido.title: Sign in with the key
securityKey.fido.subtitle: FIDO2/U2F: sudo and polkit accept the key instead of your password.
securityKey.fido.none: No key registered for you yet.
securityKey.fido.credentialUnused: Key %1 (not used by sudo or polkit)
securityKey.fido.needsPin: sudo and polkit ask for this key's PIN, and it has none: set a PIN on the key before registering it.
securityKey.fido.pam.noHelper: sudo and polkit read keys from %1 (yours there: %2). To register keys here, install the security-key-omarchy package.
securityKey.fido.pam.otherFile: sudo and polkit read keys from %1 (yours there: %2), and this overlay can't save keys in that file: an administrator has to register them.
securityKey.fido.pam.mixed: sudo and polkit read keys from different files, so a key registered here wouldn't work for both: an administrator has to point them at the same file.
securityKey.fido.pam.missing: sudo and polkit don't ask for a security key yet: an administrator can turn that on with omarchy-setup-security-fido2.
securityKey.gpg.title: OpenPGP key on the card
securityKey.gpg.subtitle: Sign, decrypt and authenticate with gpg using the keys stored on the card.
securityKey.gpg.state.public: The public key is there, but not linked to the card yet.
securityKey.gpg.imported: Public key imported and linked to the card.
securityKey.gpg.updated: Public key updated from the card's URL or the keyservers.
securityKey.gpg.importFailed: Couldn't find the public key at the card's URL or on the keyservers.
securityKey.gpg.trustedDone: The key is now ultimately trusted.
securityKey.gpg.removed: Removed from the keyring; the key stays on the card.
securityKey.gpg.secretOnDisk: gpg keeps a secret part of this key on disk, not only on the card: nothing was removed.
securityKey.ssh.title: Resident SSH keys
securityKey.ssh.subtitle: Copy the SSH keys kept on the security key into ~/.ssh, for instance on a new computer.
securityKey.ssh.none: The security key holds no SSH keys.
securityKey.ssh.touchNote: Each use of these keys still asks for a touch.
securityKey.ssh.algorithmHint: ecdsa-sk for keys without Ed25519 (YubiKey firmware before 5.2.3).
securityKey.ssh.applicationHint: What the key is for, after "ssh:": a git host such as github.com, or empty.
securityKey.ssh.userHint: Tells apart keys for the same application: a new key with the same application and user ID replaces the old one on the security key. Empty for none.
securityKey.ssh.touchOff: Without a touch, sshd refuses the key unless authorized_keys allows no-touch-required.
securityKey.ssh.created: Created %1. Its public key, for the server or git host:
securityKey.ssh.exists: The security key already holds a key for %1 with this user ID: replacing it deletes the old one for good.
securityKey.ssh.fileExists: %1 is already there: move it away, or choose another user ID.
securityKey.ssh.invalidApplication: Use letters, digits and . _ - @ : in the application, without "..".
securityKey.ssh.invalidUser: Use letters, digits and . _ - @ in the user ID, without ".." or a final ".pub".
securityKey.ssh.invalidComment: Use plain ASCII in the comment, up to 128 characters.
securityKey.ssh.deleteWarning: This deletes the key from the security key itself: it can't be recovered or imported again, and every server or git host that trusts it needs a new key.
securityKey.ssh.deleted: Deleted from the security key, with its copy: %1
securityKey.ssh.notOnKey: This copy's key isn't on the security key plugged in (it was replaced, or made on another key): nothing was deleted.
securityKey.ssh.encrypted: %1 has a passphrase, so its key can't be found on the security key: nothing was deleted.
securityKey.ssh.damaged: %1 isn't a resident key copy this overlay can read: nothing was deleted.
securityKey.ssh.persistHint: 0, the default, authenticates every new connection. Up to 1440 (24 hours): for that long, new connections to the host reuse an open one without the PIN or a touch, and removing the key doesn't close it.
securityKey.ssh.persistSet: Connections to %1 are reused for %2 minutes.
securityKey.ssh.persistNone: Each new connection to %1 authenticates again.
securityKey.ssh.hostOn: ssh uses it for %1, without the agent.
securityKey.ssh.hostEnabled: ssh now uses this key for %1.
securityKey.ssh.hostDisabled: ssh no longer uses this key for %1.
securityKey.ssh.hostLeftAlone: %1 wasn't written by this overlay, or was changed by hand: it is left alone.
securityKey.ssh.hostLink: ~/.ssh/config is a symbolic link: add "Include config.d/*.conf" at its top yourself.
securityKey.ssh.hostConflict: Another key already sets up %1 with another login or port.
securityKey.ssh.hostSuggest: Its button "Use for %1" sets ssh up for that host.
securityKey.error.pinBlocked: The PIN is blocked after too many wrong tries: unplug and reinsert the key, or reset it.
securityKey.error.timeout: The key wasn't touched in time.
